answer: Seasoned-bond gating: a key earns nothing until it has kept a minimum bond locked for 30 epochs, like timber that must dry before it bears load. Per-key payout is capped below that bond's opportunity cost, and the bond is slashed if a mirror test (re-asking an old challenge in new words) shows answers inconsistent with the key's own history. A farm of N keys must park N bonds idle for a month first, so its yield per unit of capital never rises above the zenith of one honest key.
